texts.preamble: Laxman Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand And Anr on 22 December, 2014 Author: R. R. Prasad Bench: R.R. Prasad, Ravi Nath Verma In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Cr. Appeal (D.B.) No. 857 of 2014 ... Laxman Mandal ...Appellant -V e r s u s- 1. State of Jharkhand 2. District Food Safety Officer-cum- Additional Chief Medical Officer, Deoghar ... Opposite Parties ... Coram: - Hon'Ble Mr. Justice R.R. Prasad Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ravi Nath Verma ... For the Appellant : - M/s K.P. Deo and S.K. Deo, Advocates For the State :- Addl. P.P. .... Mr. Deo, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that this appeal is directed against the order dated 01.09.2014/02.09.2014 passed in F.S.S. Case No. 27 of 2013-14 whereby and whereunder the appellant, having been found to have contravened the provisions as contained under Sections 26 & 27 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, has been sentenced to pay fine of Rs.3,00,000/-.
texts.arguments: Mr. Deo, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that this appeal is directed against the order dated 01.09.2014/02.09.2014 passed in F.S.S. Case No. 27 of 2013-14 whereby and whereunder the appellant, having been found to have contravened the provisions as contained under Sections 26 & 27 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, has been sentenced to pay fine of Rs.3,00,000/-. Being aggrieved with that order, this appeal has been preferred under Section 76 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 whereunder the appellant needs to deposit fee prescribed under the notification issued by the Central Government. Since the appellant failed to get hold of the notification no fee could be paid. Even stamp reporter could not point it out the amount which is required to be deposited. Further, it was submitted that the appeal is also barred by time by 33 days. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the appellant has preferred this appeal under Section 76 of the Food Safety and standard Act, 2006 against the order dated 2.9.2014 passed in F.S.S. case No.27 of 2013-14 whereby the appellant has been sentenced to pay fine of Rs.3,00,000/-. While preferring the appeal, it was not known to the appellant about the court fee payable and therefore, submission was made to ask the counsel appearing for the State to get hold of a notification so that it could be known about the amount which is payable.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Mr. Deo, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that this appeal is directed against the order dated 01.09.2014/02.09.2014 passed in F.S.S. Since the appellant failed to get hold of the notification no fee could be paid. Even stamp reporter could not point it out the amount which is required to be deposited. Further, it was submitted that the appeal is also barred by time by 33 days. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the appellant has preferred this appeal under Section 76 of the Food Safety and standard Act, 2006 against the order dated 2.9.2014 passed in F.S.S. case No.27 of 2013-14 whereby the appellant has been sentenced to pay fine of Rs.3,00,000/-. While preferring the appeal, it was not known to the appellant about the court fee payable and therefore, submission was made to ask the counsel appearing for the State to get hold of a notification so that it could be known about the amount which is payable.
